Guava Atole

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 6-8Prep 15 minCook 25 min

Guava Atole is a warm, comforting, and subtly sweet beverage, often enjoyed during the cooler months and especially cherished during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe. This traditional Mexican drink, thickened with masa harina, offers a delightful way to celebrate the holiday with its fragrant fruitiness, symbolizing warmth and community.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) ripe guavas, fresh or frozen
  • 4 cups (960 ml) whole milk, divided
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina (corn flour for tortillas)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
  • 1 cinnamon stick (about 3 inches/7.5 cm)
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon (optional, for garnish)

Method

  1. If using fresh guavas, wash them thoroughly, trim the ends, and cut them into quarters. If using frozen, thaw them slightly.
  2. Place the guava pieces in a blender with 1 cup (240 ml) of the milk. Blend until very smooth.
  3. Strain the guava mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a medium saucepan, pressing on the solids with a spoon to extract as much pulp as possible. Discard any seeds and fibrous material.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina with 1 cup (240 ml) of the remaining milk until no lumps remain and it forms a smooth slurry.
  5. Add the remaining 2 cups (480 ml) of milk, granulated sugar, and the cinnamon stick to the saucepan with the strained guava puree. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it just begins to simmer.
  6. Slowly pour the masa harina slurry into the simmering guava mixture in the saucepan, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
  7. Continue to cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes, or until the atole thickens to your desired consistency (it should be like a thin pudding or thick beverage). Be careful not to let it boil vigorously.
  8. Remove the cinnamon stick before serving.
  9. Serve hot, optionally garnished with a sprinkle of ground cinnamon.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, you can substitute half of the milk with evaporated milk.
  • Adjust the sugar to your preference; guavas vary in sweetness. Taste and add more if needed.
  • If the atole becomes too thick, whisk in a little more milk until it reaches the desired consistency.
